subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar adopt persistent user-configured external command hooks as a supported app, CLI, and config-file contract?
rationale: The implementation is technically credible and has direct owner hardening, but merging permanently expands CodexBar from observation and notifications into local process execution with a public event/config contract; only repository ownership can confirm that boundary.

options.title: Adopt the hook contract
options.body: Merge after final checks and explicitly support the documented disabled-by-default event, payload, configuration, CLI, and security semantics.

options.title: Narrow the initial surface
options.body: Limit the first release to a smaller event or configuration surface while preserving the same direct-exec security controls and an upgrade-compatible schema.

options.title: Decline core command execution
options.body: Close the implementation and keep external automation outside CodexBar if a persistent local-process contract is outside the product boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt the hook contract
recommendation.body: Merge after final checks and explicitly support the documented disabled-by-default event, payload, configuration, CLI, and security semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner and author of the latest hardening commits, steipete has the clearest evidence-backed authority over this product boundary.
